markingGuidanceContentItem.text: Gantt charts help project managers by showing all the tasks and when they need to be completed, making it easier to plan and meet the 12-month deadline. They also display task dependencies, so managers can identify which tasks must finish before others start. Finally, Gantt charts allow tracking progress regularly, helping to spot delays early and keep the project on schedule.

markingRubricContentItem.text: Software development approaches are a model of a general technique used to produce a software product. Through using an approach, or methodology, it provides organisation and structure to the software development. This is important in the production of quality software as it helps ensure that the key aspects of developing software (defining and understanding the problem, planning and design, implementation, testing and evaluation, and maintenance) are all sufficiently addressed without omission. Without using an approach to frame the development process, it is possible that these vital steps are missed, or not adequately addressed, resulting in a loss of quality of the finished product.

questions.title: Design and Evaluation of System Performance Using a Context Diagram (Q25, ITE 2017)

items.text:
All parts of this question refer to the following information.

A company is developing a self-serve check-in system for an airline. This allows customers who are travelling with carry-on baggage only to check-in to their flight, anytime between 1 to 24 hours before the flight, and print their boarding pass, on a computerised kiosk at the airport – rather than having to line-up at the counter to speak with an airline customer service agent.

The workflow of the system is as follows:

  • The customer arrives at the kiosk and enters the following details: first name, last name, flight number.
  • The system queries a database to check whether the details are valid and the flight departs within the next 1 to 24 hours.

- If the details are not valid, or the timeframe for the flight is outside thoselimits, a message appears on screen telling the customer to see a customer service agent for assistance. The system then exits at this point and returns to the first screen.

  • Assuming all details are valid, a screen is presented asking the customer to select their seat.
  • Once seat selection is complete, the next screen asks the customer to confirm they are not carrying any prohibited goods on the aircraft.

- If they say yes, a message appears on screen telling the customer to see a customer service agent for assistance. The system then exits at this point and returns to the first screen.

  • Assuming the customer is not carrying any prohibited goods their check-in is processed:

- Their checked-in status and seat allocation are written to a database.

- Their boarding pass is printed.

  • A thank you message appears. The system then exits at this point and returns to the first screen.
Construct a context diagram for the above scenario.

criteria.criterion: Provides a substantially correct Context Diagram, including one process for the overall system, an external entity (the customer), and all correctly labelled data flows
Provides a recognisable Context Diagram that attempts to model the described system, but with some errors and / or omissions

items.text: Identify potential performance issues with this system and suggest how these could be addressed - either in terms of addressing the issue, or improving the user experience to compensate for the issue.

criteria.criterion: Identifies legitimate possible performance issues with the system AND outlines how they could be addressed.
Identifies legitimate possible performance issues with the system OR a relevant improvement to the system.
Identifies a performance issue which could affect an information system.

sampleAnswerContentItem.text:
• Delays/latency when querying the airline databases. This could be addressed by ensuring that the system has an appropriately fast connection to the database, which is presumably stored remotely so that all check-in kiosks (and other computers operated by the airline) can access the database. Alternatively, if it is forecast that there could be a delay, which may look like the kiosk has hung or frozen, then a progress indicator (even an indeterminate indicator) should be shown on screen to indicate the system is waiting for a response from the database.
  • Time to print boarding pass. Printing a paper-based document could take longer than expected. As such, a message should be shown on screen to the user informing them what is happening, so they are not left uninformed and confused about the next steps – when in fact they are waiting for the boarding pass to be printed.

criteria.criterion: Provides a description of the role of sequential AND event-driven approaches in this game, showing an excellent understanding
Provides a description of the role of sequential AND event-driven approaches in this game, showing an excellent understanding
Provides a description of the role of sequential OR event-driven approaches in this game
Shows some understanding of sequential or event-driven approaches

sampleAnswerContentItem.text:
There are aspects of the program which are suited to a sequential approach:

  • Reading a dictionary. This doesn’t require user interaction. The code is likely to consist of opening a file, reading each line in turn into an array, then closing the file.
  • Selecting a word. This is likely to involve generating a random number, then reading the element of the array which has that random number as its index

Both of these steps can be performed as the game is loaded. Other aspects of the program suited to a sequential approach include:

  • Displaying correctly guessed letters is also a sequential process as the program should loop through the letters of the word, displaying the letters which match the guessed letter.
  • Sorting the list of players with their scores. A sorting algorithm is an example of an algorithm which doesn’t require user input.

Other aspects of the game require an event-driven approach:

  • receiving the letter guesses throughout the game. As each letter on the keyboard is pressed, this will need to be handled and then passed to a subroutine to be processed. That is, the app waits for the keypress event before progressing.
  • receiving player names from the user. As a name is entered it needs to be retrieved from the user and then processed. The app waits for the okay button’s press event to occur before processing the new name.

questions.title: Distinguish between quality assurance criteria and quality assurance management processes for this program. (Q26, ITE 2016)

items.text:
An athletics coaching company takes videos of athletes and then analyses the video in slow motion so they can work with the athlete to improve their technique.

The athletics company contracts a software development company to develop software with the following features:

  • Import video from a variety of formats
  • Play the video in slow motion
  • Allow the coach to type text-based comments which can be stored at particular timestamps in the video
  • Record audio comments from the coach which can later be played along with the video.
Distinguish between quality assurance criteria and quality assurance management processes for this program.

criteria.criterion: Shows a thorough understanding of criteria and management processes with reference to the scenario.
Shows an understanding of criteria OR management processes
Identifies a relevant criterion OR management process

sampleAnswerContentItem.text:
Criteria could include:

  • The program has good usability and is intuitive for the coaching staff.
  • The program is reliable, i.e. it doesn’t crash, text and audio comments are placed in the correct place in the video etc.
  • The documentation (user and developer) is high quality.

Management put in place strategies to ensure that each quality criteria is met. These may include:

  • Usability: management could insist that inclusivity is considered at different stages of the development process. They could also have processes for involving the client (e.g. coaching staff) in looking at prototypes/mock-ups to ensure the program will meet their needs.
  • Reliable: management could allocate resources to have testing defined early in the development process and thorough testing done after the program is created. They could also have company policies for testing during development, e.g. a programmer must test a subroutine thoroughly before it becomes part of the main program.
  • Documentation: management could develop company standards for user and developer documentation, for example how code is to be commented, how data dictionaries are used, features included in user guides etc. They could then allocate resources to ensure that the documentation meets these company standards.

A program is required to provide a range of string processing functions. The following algorithm was written by a team of developers in the early stages of development.

 

BEGIN Main

Input DataString

Display Menu

WHILE MenuOption is not 9

CASEWHERE MenuOption is

        1. : DeleteString(DataString)

        2. : ExtractString(DataString)

        3. : InsertString(DataString)

ENDCASE

Display Menu

Input MenuOption

ENDWHILE

DisplayFinal(DataString)

BEGIN DeleteString(DataString)

DataString = “”

END

 

BEGIN ExtractString(DataString)

Display “Extract String Module Called”

IF Length(DataString) = 0 THEN

Display(“ERROR: string is empty”)

END IF

END

 

BEGIN InsertString(DataString)

Display “Insert String Module Called”

END 

 

BEGIN Length(DataString)

counter = 0

IF DataString = “” THEN

return counter

ELSE

REPEAT

counter = counter + 1

Read a character from DataString

UNTIL character is end_of_string return counter

END IF

END

items.text:
The following algorithm sorts an array of names into ascending order:

BEGIN BubbleSort

        Let Last = number of names in the array

        Let Swapped = true

        WHILE Swapped = true

                Let Swapped = false

                Let i = 1

                WHILE i < Last

                        IF Name (i) > Name (i+1) THEN

                                Swap (Name (i), Name (i+1))

                                Let Swapped = true

                        ENDIF

                        Increment i

                ENDWHILE

                Decrement Last

         ENDWHILE

END BubbleSort

items.text: Compare and contrast the purpose of context diagrams and system flowcharts.

criteria.criterion: Demonstrates an excellent understanding of both Context Diagrams and System Flowcharts, indicating similarities and differences
Demonstrates a good understanding of both Context Diagrams and System Flowcharts,indicating similarities OR differences
Demonstrates some understanding of a Context Diagrams or a System Flowchart

sampleAnswerContentItem.text:
Both Context Diagrams and System Flowcharts are systems modelling tools, allowing for documentation of a system in a diagrammatic format. They each provide a different view, but when taken together provide useful diagrammatic information describing the system being modelled.

A Context Diagram is an overview of a system, and shows the data flowing between (to and from) the external entities and the system. It is at the highest level of abstraction, and does not show any detail about the processes, interfaces, logic or media used.

A Systems Flowchart shows the various sub-processes that constitute the overall system, and the hardware media that is used in inputting data to or taking data from these sub-processes. Like the context Diagram, the Systems Flowchart does not show detail of the interfaces or logic utilised in the sub-processes.

questions.title: Draw a data flow diagram to represent this system. (Q31, ITE 2016)

items.text:
A system is being developed allowing people to renew their driver’s licence over the internet.

To renew a driver’s licence, the following steps are completed:

  • The user submits their current driver’s licence number, their full name, and their date of birth.
  • The system validates this information by querying the driver’s licence database.
  • If the user is not validated (their details are not found, or do not match), an error message is returned and the user is exited from the system.
  • If the user is validated it displays their current information in the database. The user checks this information, and is able to update their address or phone number if needed.
  • Once the user confirms, or updates, their information they are prompted to submit their credit card details for payment.
  • Their credit card details are validated with an external payment processing service.
  • If their credit card is declined, an error message is returned and the user is exited from the system.
  • If their credit card is successfully processed, the driver’s licence database is updated to indicate the user has renewed and an online receipt is provided.

def HoursAndMinutes(TotalMinutes):  

    hour = TotalMinutes//60

    if hour < 1 and minute < 2:  

        print("It has been converted to: ", minute, " minute.")  

    elif hour < 2 and minute < 1:  

        print("It has been converted to: ", hour, " hour.")  

    elif hour < 2 and minute > 1:

    elif hour < 2 and minute < 2:  

        print("It has been converted to: ", hour, " hour & ", minute, " minute.")  

    else:  

        print("It has been converted to: ", hour, " hours & ", minute, " minutes.")

items.text: Explain the difference between local and global variables.

criteria.criterion: Explains Local AND global Variables well
Describes Local AND /OR global variables
Identifies a feature of a Local OR global variable

sampleAnswerContentItem.text:
The local variable is declared inside a function, whereas the Global variable is declared outside the function.

Local variables are created when the function has started execution and is lost when the function terminates, on the other hand, a Global variable is created as execution starts and is lost when the program ends.

The local variable doesn’t provide data sharing, whereas the Global variable provides data sharing.

Local variables are stored on the stack, whereas the Global variable is stored in a fixed location decided by the compiler.
